basic.name: Fehizoro Rajonhson
basic.headline: I build and maintain the systems small organisations actually run on.
basic.intro: Backend-leaning full-stack developer. I built JKA Mauritius' management platform as its sole developer — six modules in production, on FTP-only hosting with no SSH access — while completing a Master's in Software Architecture.
basic.availability: Available for freelance work and full-time roles.

howIWork: I joined JKA Mauritius' digitalisation effort on a native-PHP codebase and migrated it to Laravel while the platform stayed live for real dojo members — on shared hosting with FTP as the only access, no SSH, no staging downtime window. Every deployment decision had to survive that constraint.

That shaped how I work: I design for the environment that actually exists rather than the one that would be convenient. In practice that means caring about the parts that only show up later — data integrity, reconciliation of money, test coverage before a refactor, and being able to diagnose a failure when you cannot open a terminal on the server.

work.title: JKA Mauritius Management Platform
work.context: A national karate federation ran its administration across several dojos on spreadsheets and paper: member records, annual licences, seminar and competition registrations, and the cash each instructor collected and transferred onwards. The platform replaced that with one system used by two distinct roles — instructors managing their own dojo, administrators overseeing all of them.
work.constraints: Shared hosting with FTP as the only access: no SSH, no terminal, no Composer or Artisan on the server, no remote database connection, and no way to point the web root at Laravel's public directory.
highlights: Built six interdependent modules — members, licensing, dojos, competitions, seminars and payments — and migrated the codebase from native PHP to Laravel mid-project, without taking the platform offline.

Designed the payment flow the federation actually uses: instructors collect cash locally, submit one consolidated bank transfer with proof, and an administrator reconciles and approves it before any QR code, receipt or ticket is issued.
Set up continuous integration on GitHub Actions running the test suite against a disposable MariaDB service with synthetic fixtures, with SonarCloud static analysis on every push and pull request.
Remediated known dependency vulnerabilities identified with Snyk through a verified, zero-downtime upgrade.
Diagnosed a silent production outage with no server access by deploying single-use, token-protected diagnostic scripts, then shipped a permanent fix and a verification checklist.
Automated QR-code and ticket generation plus Excel and PDF exports, and wrote the technical handover documentation for whoever maintains the platform next.

results.label: to root cause, with no server access

work.title: UrbanHub — Validation microservice & CI/CD pipeline
work.role: Sole developer of this service, within a team project
work.context: UrbanHub models a smart city as a set of microservices communicating through events — congestion data, air quality and IoT sensor readings. I owned the validation service and everything around getting it tested, scanned, containerised and deployed.
highlights: Built the validation service with FastAPI and containerised it with Docker, running alongside the other services through Docker Compose.
Wrote a five-stage GitHub Actions pipeline: dependency install, pytest with coverage reporting, a quality stage, image build, and a staging deployment.
Wired flake8, SonarCloud analysis and Snyk dependency scanning into the quality stage, publishing every report as a build artefact.

Published the container image to GitHub Container Registry, then deployed it with Docker Compose behind a health check on the service's OpenAPI endpoint, so a broken image fails the pipeline rather than the environment.
work.note: Public repository — the pipeline and the service are there to read.
